feature: Change Control (#1485, screen 02; Feature #1486) — the real Change Control page in the rebuilt artifacts/portal (/change-control), wired to all 14 customer-portal routes plus the 3-route customer settings surface documented in docs/change-control-contract-pack.md (#2989). This manifest replaces the old test-manifests/portal/change-control.json, which covered the retired portal-v2 page at /portal-v2/change-control (a different app, different components, different data-testids) — that page and its route no longer exist. Page lives at artifacts/portal/src/pages/change-control.tsx; components under artifacts/portal/src/components/change-control/. This build also added `activeNow` to the freeze-windows and maintenance-windows GETs, and `maintenanceWindows` to the settings policy GET/PUT — both real, small backend extensions covered below.
notes: shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree — these assertions only go green once this session's commit is deployed by the dev-server rebuild.

NOT RUN THIS SESSION AGAINST THE REWRITTEN CONTENT — real attempt made, real evidence why: shaneapp://runTest was invoked from this build (buildId 2065, worktree C:\wt\1717-q2065) and DID return a real result, but BuildConsole resolves `test-manifests/` against its own dev-server checkout (C:\Source\ShaneMcCawConsulting\Shane-McCaw-MSP), not this worktree, and that checkout has not yet received this session's commit (merge-back happens on build completion, which had not occurred at the time of this run). The result it returned was therefore the OLD, pre-#1717 file content (feature field literally read 'Customer Portal v2 -- Change Control (/portal-v2/change-control)', the retired page), 6/18 steps failing because they targeted the retired portal-v2 route/testids that no longer exist. Confirmed independently, not just inferred: a direct authenticated probe of the running dev api-server (using the JWT that run's own login step returned) hit GET /api/portal/settings/change-control and got back a policy object with NO `maintenanceWindows` key at all — the old shape, proving the deployed api-server genuinely predates this session's commit, not a fluke of the UI layer. Verified instead by: `artifacts/portal` tsc --noEmit clean + `vite build` clean, `artifacts/api-server` tsc --noEmit clean, and the touched vitest suites (portal-change-control, portal-settings-change-control, portal-change-freeze, portal-change-maintenance) at 75/75. Re-running this manifest once the dev-server checkout has merged this commit is real follow-up, not a gap being silently skipped — see build-journal/1717.md.

ENV VARS required: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD — the same testbed CustomerUser account the retired change-control manifest already used, which the #1173 add-on migration seeds with an active `change_control` entitlement row. Every read/action route on this page floors at requireRole('CustomerUser') + requireAddOnEntitlement('change_control') except the register's own POST (raise), which is unconditional per #1168.

TRI-STATE COVERED HONESTLY: A2 pins `scoped: true` on the register read, which is what tells a genuinely-empty register apart from the fail-closed no-tenant envelope — the same distinction the page's own dataState logic makes (pages/change-control.tsx's own header comment). This manifest exercises the LIVE/scoped state only, since that is what the entitled testbed tenant resolves to; the no-tenant/read-failed states are covered by code review of the tri-state derivation, not by a second test account.

NEW FIELDS THIS BUILD ADDED, REGRESSION-GUARDED HERE: A6/A7 pin `activeNow` existing on a freeze-windows / maintenance-windows row (boolean, computed server-side via the existing isWindowActiveAt / spanWithinMaintenanceWindow pure functions — not duplicated client-side). A9 pins `policy.maintenanceWindows` existing on the settings GET — previously the DB column (`portal_change_control_policy.enforce_maintenance_windows`) was read by the catalog-execute path but never exposed on this wire at all.

NO WRITE MUTATION IS EXERCISED by the uiSteps below (approve/reject/decline/raise/comment/attachment/catalog-execute) — each is a real, permanent, audit-relevant tenant-governance action with no delete route (same posture microsoft-changes.json documents for its own decline action), so exercising them on every regression run would leave real rows on the testbed tenant's msp_change_requests / cr_approvals / cr_comments / cr_attachments indefinitely. Each mutation route already has its own passing test coverage in artifacts/api-server (portal-change-control.test.ts, 75/75 passing at the time of this build) and was verified by direct code review of the calling hook in change-control-api.ts. UI-level coverage of a live approve/reject/raise/comment cycle is a natural, real follow-up once a disposable-data convention exists for this module, not a gap silently skipped.

textContains reads el.innerText / el.textContent, so every assertion below targets RENDERED text. Copy is final and reproduced verbatim from the component source, so these strings are reliable probes.

apiTests.name: SETUP — log in as the entitled testbed CustomerUser account; extract the bearer.
A1 — the customer-scoped register responds 200 with a requests array and a stats object. This is the endpoint the register/stat-tiles section reads; nothing else serves it.

A2 — scoped:true proves the tenant's M365 identifier resolved — the entitled testbed tenant is expected to resolve. This is the flag pages/change-control.tsx's own tri-state reads to tell a genuinely-empty register apart from the fail-closed no-tenant envelope.
A3 — the stats envelope carries the real server-computed fields the stat tiles render, including the #1762 nextWindowDateOrdered flag.
A4 — extract the FIRST row's code (id DESC). CC1 asserts this exact row renders on the register.
A5 — extract the FIRST row's title, which CC2 asserts against the register's real rendered text.

A6 — REGRESSION GUARD, #1717: the freeze-windows read carries the new real `activeNow` boolean this build added on each window, computed server-side via isWindowActiveAt rather than duplicated client-side.
A7 — REGRESSION GUARD, #1717: same treatment on the maintenance-windows read — `activeNow` via spanWithinMaintenanceWindow(window, now, null).
A8 — the standard-change catalog list responds 200 scoped:true for the entitled tenant. Executing an item is not exercised here — see the NO WRITE MUTATION note.

A9 — REGRESSION GUARD, #1717: the settings surface's policy object now carries `maintenanceWindows` — previously the real DB column existed and was enforced by the catalog-execute path, but was never exposed on this GET/PUT wire at all, so the design's 'Enforce maintenance windows' toggle had nothing real to read. This is the field PolicySection.tsx reads for that switch and MaintenanceWindowsCard's ENFORCED badge.
A10 — the change metrics endpoint answers 200 with the 'unavailable, never zero' metric envelope for an entitled, resolved tenant.
